_meta.description: Legal procedure maps for JARVIS Legal OS. Educational only.
_meta.note: Stage text uses 'typically' or 'commonly', never 'you will' or 'you should'.

procedures.title: Claim Against a NYC Public Entity

stages.title: Incident
stages.plain: The event that caused the injury has occurred.
anticipate: Preserve evidence: photos, witness names, medical records
Request surveillance footage promptly — retention periods are short

stages.title: Notice of Claim
stages.plain: A formal notice is typically required before suing a public entity in New York.
anticipate: The notice commonly must be filed within 90 days of the incident [VERIFY]
It is typically filed with the NYC Comptroller or served on the specific agency [VERIFY]
The form asks for the date, location, description, and claimed amount
stages.typical_duration: Must typically be filed within 90 days [VERIFY]
documents: Proof of service or filing receipt
who_you_deal_with: NYC Comptroller's Office or agency counsel [VERIFY]

branches.title: Late Notice Application
branches.plain: If the 90-day window has passed, courts sometimes grant permission to file late under certain circumstances [VERIFY].

stages.title: 50-h Examination
stages.plain: After filing the notice, the public entity's attorneys typically schedule a hearing where they ask questions under oath.
anticipate: This is commonly scheduled within 90 days after the notice [VERIFY]
A court reporter typically records the testimony
An attorney is not required but is commonly recommended
stages.typical_duration: Commonly scheduled weeks to months after the notice
documents: Any documents related to the incident

stages.title: Waiting Period
stages.plain: There is typically a waiting period before a lawsuit can be filed against the public entity.
anticipate: The waiting period is commonly 30 days after the 50-h hearing [VERIFY]
During this time the claim may be adjusted or settled

branches.title: Settlement
branches.plain: A case can commonly be settled at any stage through negotiation.

stages.title: Summons & Complaint
stages.plain: A lawsuit is typically commenced by filing a summons and complaint with the court and purchasing an index number.
anticipate: Filing fees and an index number purchase are typically required
The statute of limitations for claims against public entities is commonly 1 year and 90 days from the incident [VERIFY]
stages.typical_duration: Must typically be filed within the statute of limitations

stages.title: Answer
stages.plain: The defendant typically responds to the complaint with an answer within a set time.
anticipate: The answer commonly raises defenses and may include counterclaims

stages.title: Discovery & Conferences
stages.plain: Both sides typically exchange evidence and attend court conferences to manage the case.
anticipate: Depositions, document requests, and interrogatories are common
A preliminary conference is typically scheduled by the court
This phase commonly takes several months to over a year

stages.title: Note of Issue
stages.plain: When discovery is complete, a note of issue is typically filed to place the case on the trial calendar.
anticipate: Filing the note of issue commonly signals readiness for trial

stages.title: Motions
stages.plain: Either side may file motions asking the court to decide issues before trial.
anticipate: Summary judgment motions are common — one side argues no trial is needed
Motions in limine may limit evidence at trial
stages.typical_duration: Commonly weeks to months for decisions

branches.title: Dismissal
branches.plain: The court may dismiss the case if it finds the claim lacks merit or a required step was missed.

stages.title: Settlement Conference or Trial
stages.plain: Cases commonly settle before trial through negotiation or mediation. If not, the case goes to trial.
anticipate: Settlement conferences are typically mandatory in many courts
A trial may be before a judge or jury depending on the case
Trial commonly lasts days to weeks
stages.typical_duration: Settlement possible at any point; trial commonly scheduled months after note of issue

stages.title: Judgment & Possible Appeal
stages.plain: After trial or settlement, a judgment is typically entered. Either side may appeal.
anticipate: Appeals commonly must be filed within 30 days of the judgment [VERIFY]
Collection of a judgment against a public entity follows specific rules
stages.typical_duration: Appeals commonly take months to years

procedures.title: Injury Claim Against a Private Party

stages.title: Incident
stages.plain: The event that caused the injury has occurred.
anticipate: Preserve evidence and seek medical attention promptly

stages.title: Demand or Insurance Claim
stages.plain: A demand letter or insurance claim is commonly the first step toward resolution.
anticipate: The at-fault party's insurance company typically handles the claim
An adjuster may contact you for a recorded statement
stages.typical_duration: Commonly weeks to months for response

stages.title: Summons & Complaint
stages.plain: If the claim cannot be resolved, a lawsuit is typically filed in court.
anticipate: The statute of limitations for personal injury in NY is commonly 3 years [VERIFY]
stages.typical_duration: Must be filed within the statute of limitations

stages.title: Answer
stages.plain: The defendant typically responds with an answer.

stages.title: Discovery
stages.plain: Both sides typically exchange evidence through depositions, documents, and interrogatories.
anticipate: This phase commonly takes several months

stages.title: Note of Issue
stages.plain: Filed when discovery is complete to place the case on the trial calendar.

stages.title: Motions
stages.plain: Either side may file motions before trial.
anticipate: Summary judgment motions are common

stages.title: Settlement or Trial
stages.plain: Most cases commonly settle. If not, the case proceeds to trial.

stages.title: Judgment
stages.plain: A judgment is entered after trial or settlement.

stages.title: Incident
stages.plain: The event giving rise to the claim has occurred.
anticipate: Gather evidence and calculate damages

stages.title: Filing with the Clerk
stages.plain: A small claims case is typically started by filing with the court clerk and paying a small fee.
anticipate: The claim limit in NYC Small Claims is commonly $10,000 [VERIFY]
Filing can typically be done in person at the courthouse

stages.title: Service by the Court
stages.plain: The court typically serves the defendant by mail with notice of the hearing date.
anticipate: The hearing is commonly scheduled several weeks after filing

stages.title: Hearing
stages.plain: Both sides typically present their case to an arbitrator or judge in an informal setting.
anticipate: Bring all evidence, documents, and witnesses
No formal rules of evidence — the arbitrator commonly asks questions directly

stages.title: Decision
stages.plain: The arbitrator or judge typically issues a decision, sometimes the same day.
anticipate: Decisions are commonly mailed within a few days
stages.typical_duration: Commonly same day to a few weeks

stages.title: Collecting a Judgment
stages.plain: If you win, collecting the judgment is typically your responsibility.
anticipate: The court does not commonly collect for you
Enforcement options may include wage garnishment or bank restraint [VERIFY]

stages.title: Gather Facts
stages.plain: Collect and preserve all evidence, documents, and information related to your situation.
anticipate: Write down what happened while it is fresh
Take photos, save texts and emails, note witnesses

stages.title: Talk to Legal Help
stages.plain: Contact a licensed attorney, legal aid organization, or court help center for guidance on your situation.
anticipate: Many organizations offer free consultations
A lawyer can explain deadlines that may apply

stages.title: Formal Claim or Filing
stages.plain: Depending on the situation, a formal claim, complaint, or filing is typically required to start the legal process.
anticipate: Deadlines vary widely by type of claim
Some claims require a notice before a lawsuit can be filed

stages.title: Response
stages.plain: The other side typically has an opportunity to respond to the claim.

stages.title: Resolution
stages.plain: The matter is typically resolved through negotiation, mediation, hearing, or trial.
anticipate: Many matters settle without a trial
